item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot app: Updates to Home and navigation
item.description:
Updated November 11, 2026: We have updated the workspaces timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why]

In MC1479277 about updates to the Microsoft Copilot app, we introduced Home as the new starting point that brings Chat and Cowork together, so users can get chat assistance and delegate multi-step tasks in one view. This post builds on that announcement with worldwide rollout timing and the addition of Projects and Workspaces to the Home experience. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • Standard release begins late October 2026
  • Deferred release begins late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of the Microsoft Copilot app. Access to Cowork and Cowork-related capabilities depends on Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and your organization’s usage-based billing configuration. 

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot web, desktop, and mobile app.

What will happen

Projects:

  • In addition to what was communicated in MC1479277, Projects provides a dedicated space in Home for organizing related chats, Cowork tasks, and everything they share: files, instructions, and outputs. From there they can create a new project, add files and context, and start chats or Cowork tasks inside it. Responses are grounded in the project's context first, then in the user's broader Microsoft 365 work context. Projects are accessible from the Home navigation pane.
  • Projects doesn't store content itself, and files stay in OneDrive under the same permissions, sensitivity labels and retention policies you already use. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files that Copilot creates are saved to the user's OneDrive.
  • Projects are available on Windows, Mac, & Web apps across tier 1 languages. It is coming soon to mobile apps.

Workspaces:

  • Users will see "Notebooks" become "Workspaces" in the left navigation of the Copilot app as Copilot Notebooks evolves into Copilot Workspaces. Workspaces give teams a shared space to bring together context, team members, and working files to work alongside Copilot on an ongoing workstream.
  • Existing notebooks will convert into “workspaces,” retaining all previously added or made content. Read FAQs on our Support Page.
  • This change will roll out to all users with access to Copilot Notebooks first in the Frontier program. Workspaces will rollout to standard release by January 2027, and deferred release by February 2027. Access to individual capabilities in Copilot Workspaces will vary by license.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Review which users are included in a spending policy that grants Cowork access and confirm your intended usage-based billing configuration.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Windows: Updates to address compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
item.description:
Updated November 11, 2026: On November 16, 2026, an update will be released for Microsoft Edge and WebView2, delivered via the PKI Metadata component, which will fully remove default trust for the remaining roots (emSign Root CA - G1, emSign Root CA - C1, emSign ECC Root CA, and emSign Root TLS CA - G1). Devices check for PKI Metadata updates every 10 hours and shortly after each new app launch. 

For more information, see Microsoft Response to eMudhra Certificate Authority Key Compromise.

[What and why]

Microsoft is responding to an issue involving eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority (CA) private keys, six associated with TLS and two with code signing. Because these keys could be recovered, they could potentially be used to create certificates or sign content that appeared to come from a trusted CA. The issue arose in eMudhra's certificate hierarchy and was not a compromise of Microsoft systems.

Microsoft is updating certificate trust to block affected certificate authorities and remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Windows, Microsoft Edge, or WebView2, particularly organizations with certificates that chain to one of the eight certificates being removed
  • Organizations managing disconnected Windows devices or disconnected Azure devices may need to take additional action

Platforms and services

  • Windows
  • Microsoft Edge
  • WebView2
  • Azure virtual machines

What will happen

  • Microsoft has published an update to the Windows Disallowed Certificate Trust List to block the affected certificate authorities.
  • Microsoft has deployed a separate CRLSet update for Microsoft Edge and WebView2 to block affected TLS certificates signed by the affected certificate authorities.
  • The Microsoft Edge and WebView2 update is delivered automatically through the component update mechanism. Customers do not need to install a new browser version.
  • Microsoft has released updates to Windows and Microsoft Edge to remove certificates associated with the affected hierarchies from their trust lists.
  • After these updates reach a device, the affected certificates will no longer be trusted by default through the respective trust lists.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • Keep updates flowing. Allow automatic Windows certificate trust updates and Microsoft Edge component updates to reach your devices.
  • Check disconnected Windows devices. If you manage Windows devices that do not receive automatic updates, make sure your update process delivers the updated Disallowed Certificate Trust List and upcoming trust-list changes. See the Microsoft Learn guidance in Learn more for information about distributing certificate trust lists in disconnected environments.
  • Review disconnected Azure devices. Review disconnected Azure devices running on Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) or single-instance VMs. Updated images are available in Azure Marketplace, and customers can deploy them to protect against this vulnerability.
  • Replace dependent certificates. If any of your certificates chain to one of the seven certificates being removed, identify those dependencies and obtain replacement certificates or an alternative trusted chain before the changes reach your devices.

Learn more

  • Microsoft’s response to compromised eMudhra certificate authority keys
  • Configure trusted roots and disallowed certificates in Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) New Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service experiences across Teams, Copilot, and Outlook
item.description:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing new Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service experiences that bring customer context, business processes, and agent capabilities into Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Outlook, and other Microsoft 365 applications. These updates help sellers and service representatives access customer information, take actions, and collaborate without switching between applications.

The release includes:

  • Sales and Service skills for Copilot experiences such as Cowork, Code, and Autopilot
  • Dynamics 365 CRM integration with Teams Channel Agent
  • Sales Development Agent

[Rollout schedule]

Beginning October 8, 2026: 

  • Dynamics 365 Sales and Dynamics 365 Service skills for Copilot experiences:
    • General Availability (Cowork)
    • Frontier (Code)
    • Private Preview (Autopilot)
  • Dynamics 365 CRM in the flow of Teams enters Public Preview.
  • Sales Development Agent enters Public Preview (Frontier enablement continues to be required until December 1).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using or evaluating Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, Microsoft Teams, or Microsoft 365 Copilot, and administrators responsible for agent deployment.

Platforms and services

  • Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 Apps
  • Outlook
  • Cowork
  • Code
  • Autopilot

What will happen

Sales and Service Skills for Cowork, Autopilot, and Code (General Availability for Cowork, Frontier program for Code, and Private Preview for Autopilot)

Thirty sales and service skills package Dynamics 365 business expertise into reusable building blocks for Cowork, Autopilot, and Code. These skills help sellers and service representatives identify opportunities and risks, update CRM data, resolve service issues, and take actions grounded in customer data and business processes. Organizations can also use these skills with custom agents to support workflows enterprises build themselves. Learn more about the Sales and Service skills.

Dynamics 365 CRM in the flow of Teams (Public Preview)

Dynamics 365 CRM in the flow of Teams helps sellers and service representatives work from shared customer context in Teams conversations, bringing customer updates and supported actions into the channel so they can collaborate on accounts and cases without switching applications. Learn more about the Channel Agent for Microsoft Teams and how to use it with Dynamics 365 CRM.

  • Deployment requires licensing for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Microsoft Teams.
  • Requires administrator activation of the Channel Agent.

Sales Development Agent (Public Preview, Frontier enablement continues to be required until December 1).

Sales Development Agent helps sellers build and qualify pipeline by researching prospects, personalizing outreach, managing follow-up conversations, and advancing qualified opportunities before handing them to a seller. It is managed in Teams, sends email from its own Exchange account, and can connect to customer-authorized CRM platforms. Learn more about the Sales Development Agent and review deployment guidance

  • Beginning December 1, 2026, Sales Development Agent will be billed on usage-based billing through Copilot Credits. Additional details, including consumption estimates and licensing guidance, will be shared closer to the transition date.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required unless your organization plans to deploy or continue using these capabilities.

To prepare:

  • Configure spending policies for applicable AI experiences before December 1, 2026. 
  • Review deployment guidance for Sales Development Agent prior to activation. 
  • Review deployment guidance and prerequisites for Teams Channel Agent. 
  • Communicate billing and deployment requirements to administrators responsible for Copilot and Dynamics 365 environments.

Learn more

  • Activate Sales Development agent (preview) | Microsoft Learn
  • Sales Development agent overview | Microsoft Learn
  • Set up a Channel Agent for Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Use Channel Agent | Microsoft Support
  • Use Dynamics 365 Customer Service skills in Copilot Cowork | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Introduces new agent-based experiences including Sales Development Agent, Sales and Service skills, and Dynamics 365 CRM integration in Teams.
Does the change provide users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Dynamics 365 sales and service capabilities through Copilot experiences, Teams Channel Agent, and Sales Development Agent.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Dynamics 365 customer data becomes accessible within Teams, Copilot, and Microsoft 365 experiences to support customer workflows and agent actions.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators must activate Channel Agent, and Sales Development Agent.
Can users enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. Use of the experiences depends on administrator enablement, licensing, and policy assignment. Administrators remain the primary control point.

item.title: [planForChange] Copilot Studio - Set up third-party agent connections in conversations
item.description:
We are announcing improvements to the experience of setting up connections in chats with Copilot Studio agents. These improvements will reach general availability by December 31, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Previously, users needed to leave their conversation, go to a separate connection-management experience, complete setup, and then restart their interaction. This feature is introducing a more seamless way for users to connect agents to third-party services. When an agent requires a connection, users will be guided through a focused setup experience without leaving the conversation or being redirected to the full connection-management portal. When possible, the agent will reuse an existing valid connection.

With this update:
  • Users can establish a required third-party connection from their agent conversation.
  • Users complete only the setup required for the service they are using.
  • Users return directly to the conversation after connecting.
  • An eligible existing connection can be reused instead of configuring another connection.
  • Users can continue working with connected agents across Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat.
  • Existing organizational controls that govern which connectors and connections users can access will continue to determine availability.
Please note that developers of agents published through a custom web UI using the Standard harness will be required to make changes to support the new connection experience.

What action do I need to take?
To prepare for this change, we recommend that you:
  • Inform support teams and agent users about the improved connection experience.
  • Review your existing organizational controls for connectors and connections.
For agents published through a custom web UI using the Standard harness, update your implementation to:
  • Open the new connection window.
  • Continue the conversation after connection setup succeeds.
If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Support connection setup in a custom canvas.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat: Filter responses by content source
item.description:
[What and why]

We're introducing content source filters in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. This feature allows users to scope a prompt to specific content sources so that Copilot grounds its response only in the sources they select. This helps users focus responses on the most relevant Microsoft 365 content, as well as connected or available third-party sources, while maintaining existing permission and access controls.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat

What will happen

  • Users will see a source selection control in the Copilot Chat prompt area.
  • Users can select one or more available content sources to limit retrieval and grounding for a specific prompt to those sources.
  • Available sources reflect the content sources enabled in your tenant, including Graph connectors and federated connectors available to users.
  • This feature changes where Copilot retrieves information for a prompt and does not change what content a user is permitted to access. Data access, compliance boundaries, and tenant data handling remain unchanged.
  • If no source is selected, Copilot Chat behavior remains unchanged and will use its default orchestration across available sources.
  • Responses will continue to include citations that reflect the selected sources.
  • Source selection applies only to the current prompt and does not persist across sessions.
  • This feature is enabled by default for users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Copilot source selection

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Review the display names of published Graph connectors, ensuring that they are clear and recognizable, as these names will appear in the source selection experience for users.
  • Verify the health and search permissions of connectors that should be available to users. Connectors in an error or unpublished state will not appear.

[Learn more]

  • Control and review sources of Microsoft Copilot Chat's responses | Microsoft Support

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Outlook: Update to default blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy
item.description:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

To enhance security in Outlook on the web and new Outlook for Windows, we are updating the default list of blocked file types in OwaMailboxPolicy. As part of this update, the .msix and .msixbundle file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in the default OWA Mailbox policy and any custom policies created in your tenant. Most organizations are not expected to be affected by this update because these file types are infrequently used. This update is part of our ongoing efforts to strengthen security and help protect organizations from potentially unsafe file attachments.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Rollout begins in early December 2026 (previously early November) and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November).

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Exchange Online administrators who manage OWA mailbox policies
  • Users who send or receive .msix or .msixbundle attachments in Outlook on the web or new Outlook for Windows

Platforms and services

  • Outlook for the web
  • New Outlook for Windows
  • Exchange Online

What will happen

  • The .msix and .msixbundle file types will be added to the BlockedFileTypes list in all OWA Mailbox policies in your organization, including the default policy and any custom policies created in your tenant.
  • Users who send or receive .msix or .msixbundle attachments in Outlook on the web or new Outlook for Windows will no longer be able to open or download them.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if your organization does not rely on the .msix or .msixbundle file types. If your organization relies on these file types, we recommend that you add them to the AllowedFileTypes property of your users' OwaMailboxPolicy objects prior to rollout.

[Learn more]

  • Blocked attachments in Outlook | Microsoft Support
  • Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -AllowedFileTypes | Microsoft Learn
  • Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -BlockedFileTypes | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Malicious QR code detection in messages
item.description:
Updated November 10, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is extending malicious URL protection to provide near-real-time detection of malicious destinations embedded in QR codes shared in messages. Teams will analyze QR code destinations to identify potential phishing and fraud threats and display an additional warning when malicious content is detected.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously mid-November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who use Microsoft Teams messaging

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams chats, meeting chats, and channels

What will happen

  • Teams will decode and evaluate QR code destinations in inline images shared in 1:1 chats, group chats, meeting chats, and channels.
  • Detection applies to internal and external communications.
  • Images containing QR codes from external senders are already blurred by default. When Teams identifies a malicious QR code, users will also see the warning, “This message contains a link that might be harmful,” and a “Learn about file and link safety” link.
  • QR code images from internal senders are not blurred by default. The same warning will appear when Teams detects a malicious QR code.
  • For users on Teams mobile in China, QR code images are blurred by default regardless of whether the sender is internal or external, and any messages containing malicious QR code will be blocked.
  • Malicious QR code detection is managed by the existing Malicious URL protection setting.
  • The setting is enabled by default. Organizations with Malicious URL protection enabled will automatically receive malicious QR code detection as the feature rolls out.
  • No separate configuration is available or required for malicious QR code detection.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Admins can review or change the existing Malicious URL protection setting in Teams admin center > Settings and policies > Messaging Safety.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users and help desk staff about the additional warning for detected malicious QR codes.
  • Clarify that QR code blurring is a separate precautionary experience and does not mean that Teams has identified a QR code as malicious.
  • Review internal documentation about Teams messaging security and update it if necessary.

Learn more

(Both to be updated closer to rollout.)

  • Make sure chats, links, and files are secure in Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Support
  • Malicious URL protection in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Automatic recording and transcription options align with admin policies
item.description:

This change reduces confusion, improves policy compliance, and helps ensure organizers cannot select options that are unavailable based on organizational settings.

  • Teams administrators who manage meeting recording and transcription policies
  • Meeting organizers who configure automatic recording or transcription settings in Meeting options

Platforms and services

  • Teams desktop, web, and mobile clients that support Meeting Options.

What will happen

  • Meeting organizers will only see automatic recording and transcription options allowed by their effective Teams meeting policy.
  • Policy evaluation respects policies assigned directly to a user, inherited through group assignment, or applied through the global policy.
  • A new Record only option will be available when recording is permitted by policy.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Video sharing from OneDrive in Teams events

[What and why]

Microsoft Teams will soon support sharing video directly from OneDrive during Teams events. Organizers and producers using Manage what attendees see can load videos from OneDrive and present them on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos in PowerPoint. This improvement provides smoother, higher-quality video playback for attendees and simplifies event production through built-in video playback controls.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and end in early December 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Teams event organizers and producers using events configured with Manage what attendees see.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • OneDrive
  • Teams events

What will happen

  • Organizers and producers will be able to select and share videos stored in OneDrive directly within Teams events configured with Manage what attendees see and will have access to built-in controls to start and pause video playback during events.
  • Videos can be presented on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos into a PowerPoint presentation.
  • Attendees will experience smoother and higher-quality video playback.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

item.title: [planForChange] Discover usage-based billing (UBB) experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot
item.description:
[What and why:]

As previously announced in MC1479277, we are making usage-based experiences in the Microsoft Copilot app easier to discover. Usage-based billing experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot, will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, even if their organization has not enabled access. Users without an applicable spending policy will see an option to request access or learn more, based on their organization's settings.

Based on customer feedback, we are extending the rollout timeline and introducing an additional admin control that will allow organizations to provide custom guidance to users. These changes give administrators more time to prepare and greater flexibility to manage how users discover and request access to usage-based experiences.

[Rollout schedule:]

The updated rollout schedule is as follows:

  • Mid-November 2026: The new admin setting, "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences," will become available for administrators to configure.
  • Mid-December 2026: An additional option will be introduced to the admin setting, allowing administrators to provide a custom URL as part of the Learn more informational experience that directs users to their own organization’s guidance. The option will be available if you select "Specific users" or “No users” in the setting.
  • End of January 2027: The new discoverability behavior and admin setting will be enforced. The old setting "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing" will be retired. This will apply to customers on deferred release at the end of February 2027.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: 

  • Organizations with users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Platforms/services: 

  • Microsoft Copilot app and Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • Entry points for Cowork, Code, and Autopilot will be visible by default to licensed users starting at the end of January 2027.
  • Users without an applicable spending policy giving them access to the feature will see an informational experience with an option to "Request access" or "Learn more," depending on their how their organization has configured the new "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences" admin setting.
  • Administrators can configure which users are eligible to request access, including the option to prevent access requests.
  • Administrators will be able to provide a custom URL directing users to organizational guidance. Only users who cannot request access will see the secondary URL, "Your organization’s guidance", as part of the Learn more informational experience.  
  • The existing setting, "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing," will continue to apply until it is retired at the end of January 2027.

Examples of the customizable “Your organization’s guidance” link on the informational experience for Cowork and Code. UI subject to change.

This change does not automatically enable usage-based experiences or initiate billing. Users must have an applicable spending policy and available Copilot Credits before they can use these experiences.

[Action required / recommendations:]

We recommend that administrators:

  1. Review the new setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings > Access requests to usage-based billing experiences when it becomes available in mid-November. Starting mid-December, you will be able to configure a custom URL in this setting for users who you decide cannot request access.
  2. Configure access request preferences to determine which users can request access to usage-based experiences.
  3. Prepare organizational guidance and, beginning in mid-December, configure a custom URL if you want to direct users to information specific to your organization.
  4. Review spending policies to ensure that access to usage-based experiences aligns with your organization's requirements.

We recommend reviewing and configuring these settings before the new discoverability behavior is enforced at the end of January 2027.

Learn more: Access requests to usage-based billing experiences (This will be updated in mid-Dec to reflect instructions for the custom URL once available in the setting)

[Compliance considerations:]

This update introduces additional administrative controls for managing access requests and organizational guidance. It does not automatically grant users access to usage-based experiences or change existing spending policy requirements.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Simplifying AI access: Introducing usage-based billing
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the rollout scope and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

The new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business combines everyday AI through a user subscription license with Advanced AI through usage-based billing. Beginning in mid-November, 2026, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants. This phased approach makes it easier for new customers to access eligible usage-based AI experiences, including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities, while reducing billing complexity and preserving flexibility to expand usage over time based on business needs. 

This change will not apply to your existing Microsoft 365 tenant as part of the November rollout. We will share additional information before making usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants. If you’d like to get started sooner, you can enable usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

What is changing 

  • Eligible purchases made by new tenants: Beginning in mid-November, pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business and Microsoft 365 Business with Copilot purchases made by new tenants. 
  • If the new tenant does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy, they will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup. 
  • The resulting spending policy will have a spending limit of 4,000 Copilot credits per user per month, with charges based on actual usage. 
  • Charges apply only when these experiences are used, subject to the usage controls and spending limits established by the administrator. 
  • We will begin rolling out this change to eligible customers in supported markets. The change will not initially be available in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, the Netherlands, Poland, or Spain. We plan to include these markets in the next phase of the rollout in early 2027, with additional details and timing to be shared closer to launch. 

What is not changing 

  • Your existing Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscription benefits and payment terms do not change.
  • Usage-based billing will not be configured by default for your existing tenant as part of the November rollout. 
  • If your organization already has a spending policy configured, the existing spending policy remains in place. 

When this will happen 

  • Mid-November 2026: Usage-based billing default-on will begin for eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants directly from Microsoft, including through Microsoft web. 
  • Existing tenants: We plan to make usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants across all markets beginning in early 2027. We’ll share more details, including specific timing and what to expect, closer to launch. 
  • Optional action: Existing tenants can turn on usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Starting in early 2027: The change applies to eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made through Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) channels, with specific timing to be shared closer to launch. 

How usage-based billing works 

  • When usage-based billing is configured, the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy support access to eligible usage-based experiences. 
  • If you want to turn on usage-based billing for your existing tenant, you can create and manage a spending policy through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Your organization can adjust its spending policies and controls to align with its needs. Disabling usage-based billing prevents access to experiences that require it. 

What you can do to prepare 

  • Review which eligible usage-based experiences—including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities—may support your organization’s needs. 
  • Review your organization’s usage-based billing, governance, and cost-management requirements. 
  • If you choose to turn on usage-based billing ahead of this update, you can create or adjust usage controls and spending policies in Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

Learn more 

  • Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center: https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/copilot/costmanagement/overview 
  • Usage-based billing and cost management for Copilot Credits: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

Microsoft 365 Copilot is introducing legal plugins in Word and Cowork. These plugins provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents. They can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources, helping legal professionals complete legal work in the Microsoft 365 experiences they already use.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout began in late April 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot commercial licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Word desktop
  • Cowork

What will happen

  • Legal plugins in Copilot provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
  • The plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources.
  • The legal capabilities include more than 20 purpose-built legal skills.
  • In Word desktop, the legal plugin is enabled by default. When enabled, Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks in Word.
  • In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks.
  • The legal skills can help users review contracts against playbooks, draft contracts using templates and precedent agreements, compare contracts with precedents, templates, and policies, and explain tracked changes.
  • The Legal Agent is being retired. Existing Legal Agent users will lose access to the product.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin setup is required.

If your organization plans to use the legal plugins:

  • Ensure Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are assigned to eligible users.
  • Review internal legal workflows that may benefit from these capabilities.
  • Communicate these capabilities to your legal teams.
  • Update internal documentation or help desk guidance as appropriate.
  • Instruct legal team users to add the legal plugin in Cowork.
  • Instruct legal team users to use legal skills in Copilot in Word desktop.

If your organization does not plan to use the legal plugins:

  • Turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center to disable the legal plugin in Word for all users.
  • Turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center to disable the plugin in Cowork for all users.

Learn more

  • Manage Copilot for legal - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. The legal plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 to support legal tasks. The supplied source does not specify changes to data storage or caching.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Legal capabilities previously released as the Legal Agent are being made available as legal plugins in Word and Cowork. They provide purpose-built legal skills and can use work context from Microsoft 365.
Does the change provide users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can use purpose-built legal skills in Copilot in Word and Cowork to summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
Does the change add integration with third-party software products?Yes. The legal plugins can connect to supported third-party legal sources. The supplied sources do not identify specific third-party products.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins can turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The supplied source does not specify whether these controls support Entra ID group membership.
Does the change allow a user to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before using its legal skills. The supplied source does not state that users can independently disable the Word legal plugin.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot Feedback UX update
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

We’re updating the thumbs-down feedback experience in Microsoft Copilot to make it easier for users to provide specific, actionable feedback. Today, many thumbs-down responses are submitted without comments, providing sentiment but limited information about the issue. When users select thumbs down, they’ll be able to select one or more feedback categories and optionally provide additional comments, giving each categorized response a signal that can be routed to the appropriate team or issue type.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users who can submit feedback in supported Microsoft Copilot experiences may see the updated thumbs-down feedback form. The planned audience includes users signed in with Microsoft Entra ID organizational accounts, users signed in with consumer Microsoft accounts, and users in Education tenants. The feature isn’t currently planned for Mobile, GCC, GCC High, DoD, or other sovereign cloud environments.

The updated feedback experience is planned for Microsoft Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Edge, Copilot in Microsoft Outlook, and Copilot in Microsoft Teams, across web browsers, Windows, and macOS. The WXPN/Catalyst experience isn’t currently included.

When a user selects thumbs down on a Copilot response, they may see selectable categories describing the issue, can select more than one category, and can optionally enter additional feedback in a free-text field. The thumbs-up feedback experience isn’t changing. This update applies only to the existing “Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft” admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged. During the controlled rollout, some users will continue to see the existing feedback experience.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required for this change. It will be visible to users who are already allowed to submit feedback under the existing policy.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Yes. When a user chooses to submit thumbs-down feedback, the selected categories, optional free-text comment, and optional screenshot are new data captured as part of that submission.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. This UX change applies to the existing "Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft" admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Rewrite with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat coming soon to Edge for Business users

Microsoft Edge for Business will soon support Writing Assistance, a new feature powered by Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. This capability helps users draft and rephrase editable text directly within Edge, enhancing productivity and writing quality. Users can access Writing Assistance by highlighting editable text and right-clicking to open the context menu.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 420335.

When this will happen

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling late January 2027 (previously end of October 2026) and expect to complete rollout by late January 2027 (previously late October).

  • Writing Assistance will be enabled by default for Edge for Business users. 
  • Users can access Writing Assistance by highlighting editable text and right-clicking to open the context menu.
  • If Microsoft 365 Copilot is restricted from accessing page content due to Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies, Writing Assistance will not function on that content.
  • Admins can manage this feature using the InlineComposeEnabled policy setting.

What you can do to prepare

No admin action is required before rollout.

We recommend:

  • Reviewing your current DLP configurations to understand how they may impact Writing Assistance functionality.
  • Notifying users about this new capability.
  • Updating internal documentation to reflect this change.

Learn more about how DLP affects Copilot access to page content: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Edge and Access to Page Content | Microsoft Edge | Microsoft Learn

Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Copilot Chat by highlighting editable text and using the right-click context menu to access Writing Assistance, enabling AI-assisted drafting and rephrasing.
Does the change modify Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies or enforcement?Yes. If DLP policies restrict Copilot from accessing page content, the Writing Assistance feature will not function on that content.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Gov rollout of this feature is still paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by late November 2026 (previously early November) via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and November 23, 2026 (previously November 3) for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available. 

[Additional information:]

  • Migration guide: Migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy for sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips.
  • Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy Microsoft Graph API Overview
  • Exchange Online EWS, Your Time is Almost Up
  • Deprecation of EWS in Exchange Online 
  • Enhancing Microsoft 365 security by eliminating high-privilege access 
  • Blog Post: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing are moving to Cross-Tenant Access Policy

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint: Annotate sensitivity-label protected PDFs on the web
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft OneDrive and SharePoint on the web will support annotation for PDFs encrypted with Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels. Users who have the appropriate editing usage rights will be able to annotate protected PDFs in their browser without removing the sensitivity label. The file's sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights will be preserved when changes are saved.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late January 2027 and expected to complete in late January 2027

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • OneDrive for Business and SharePoint customers
  • This feature does not apply to OneDrive Consumer.

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Business and SharePoint on the web
  • All browsers are supported.

What will happen

  • Users who have editing usage rights can annotate sensitivity label-protected, encrypted PDFs in the OneDrive or SharePoint web PDF viewer.
  • Available annotation tools include ink, highlight, free text, notes, signatures, image/shape/date stamps, bookmarks, and form fields.
  • Users can save annotations without removing the sensitivity label.
  • The sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights are preserved when the annotated PDF is saved.
  • Users with view-only rights will continue to see the PDF as read-only and cannot annotate.
  • This change does not grant users additional access or editing rights.
  • No feature-specific admin control or configuration is required. Existing sensitivity label and usage-rights settings determine who can view or edit protected PDFs.

[Action required and recommendations]

No feature-specific admin action is required to enable this update.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users who routinely review labeled or regulated documents that they can annotate protected PDFs in place.
  • Confirm that your sensitivity label and usage-rights configuration reflects who should be able to edit or view protected PDFs.
  • Update internal documentation and helpdesk guidance as appropriate.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is accessed or modified?Yes. Users with existing editing usage rights gain a new way to modify protected PDFs by adding annotations in the OneDrive or SharePoint web PDF viewer.
Does the change preserve Information Protection label behavior?Yes. Users can annotate PDFs protected by sensitivity labels without removing the label. The sensitivity label, encryption, and usage rights are preserved when the file is saved.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Purview: Retirement of select DSPM partner integrations
item.description:
[What and why]

Effective December 7, 2026, we will retire the public preview experience for select non-Microsoft data sources in Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) through partner integrations.

The affected partner integrations are Varonis for Salesforce data, BigID for Databricks, Cyera for Snowflake, and OneTrust for Google Cloud Platform (GCP). We are evolving Microsoft Purview and rethinking how we bring non-Microsoft signals into the Purview experience.

This change applies only to the partner integrations listed above. Other Microsoft Purview DSPM capabilities are not affected.

[Rollout schedule]

The affected partner integrations will no longer be available beginning December 7, 2026.

This change applies to:

  • Worldwide
  • GCC
  • GCC High
  • DoD

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations participating in the public preview for connecting supported non-Microsoft data sources to Microsoft Purview DSPM through the affected partner integrations

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management (DSPM)

What will happen

Beginning December 7, 2026:

  • Organizations will no longer be able to connect the supported non-Microsoft data sources to Microsoft Purview DSPM through the affected partner integrations.
  • Data from those sources will no longer be ingested, processed, or displayed in Microsoft Purview DSPM through these integrations.
  • Other Microsoft Purview DSPM capabilities are not affected.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

If your organization currently uses these integrations, we recommend reviewing related internal processes or dependencies and updating them as needed before December 7, 2026.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform admin center – New feedback form default policy
item.description:
We are announcing the ability for administrators to control the default settings on the feedback forms displayed to users when they submit feedback to us in Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Copilot Studio. This feature will reach general availability on November 16, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This new policy adds two new settings, that control the default checkbox status presented to end users who submit Microsoft feedback:
  • Default for Content and Context Sharing – When enabled, the "include screenshot and other context" box is checked by default.
  • Default for Email Sharing – When enabled the box to allow Microsoft to contact users regarding their feedback is checked by default.
In addition, the default setting for these fields will now default to "Enabled."

This new policy does not change or override your existing feedback settings in "Product Feedback," "Basic Copilot Feedback," and "Additional Copilot Feedback" and only applies if these settings (or sub-settings within) are enabled. If an admin has disabled any of the underlying feedback or sharing options, the new defaults have no effect on them, and the existing restriction stays in place.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Changes to custom organizational data in MODS for Workforce Insights
item.description:
[What and why]

We're changing how the Workforce Insights agent receives custom organizational data from Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service (MODS). The separate Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS will be retired. Going forward, organizational data will reach the Workforce Insights agent through the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint. The Workforce Insights agent is part of the Microsoft Frontier program and is currently in preview.

Ingestion of custom public attributes through Microsoft 365 profile is already generally available. For custom non-public attributes, customers who currently use the Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS or wish to enable this capability for the first time, must join the private preview.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Workforce Insights endpoint retirement (Frontier preview) in MODS: Starting November 18, 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizational Data Source Administrators in organizations that send custom attributes to the Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS
  • Organizations that plan to use custom attributes in Copilot experiences and the Workforce Insights Agent
  • If your organization doesn't send custom attributes to the Workforce Insights endpoint today, no immediate action is required

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service
  • Microsoft 365 profile
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Workforce Insights agent

What will happen

  • After November 18, 2026, the Workforce Insights endpoint will no longer be available as a destination in MODS. To ingest custom public attributes, use the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint in MODS.
  • To bring custom non-public attributes (such as job level) into Copilot experiences and the Workforce Insights Agent, your organization must join the private preview.
  • Your current Workforce Insights endpoint selection won’t carry over. You must explicitly select the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint in MODS.
  • Data previously uploaded to the Workforce Insights endpoint will remain stale and continue to serve the Workforce Insights Agent and organizational queries in Copilot. You won't be able to upload subsequent data through the retired endpoint. See how to manage your data in MODS documentation in the Learn more section below.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization currently sends custom non-public attributes to the Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS, complete these actions before November 18, 2026:

  • Identify what attributes you ingest to Workforce Insights endpoint today. Ingest updated public attributes using Microsoft 365 profile endpoint in MODS. 
  • For non-public attributes, request to join the private preview by contacting wficomm@microsoft.com. Work with privacy and data governance stakeholders to determine the access policy and then ingest data to the Microsoft 365 profile endpoint. Keep in mind that these attributes will also be available to Copilot experiences as capabilities continue to roll out, not only the Workforce Insights Agent.
  • Don't select the Workforce Insights endpoint for new uploads, even if it's still available when your preview starts.
  • Complete the switch before November 18, 2026.

Learn more

  • Overview of Workforce Insights Agent
  • Introduction to Microsoft 365 Organizational Data Service 
  • Import and manage your organizational data with a .csv file - Microsoft 365 Apps | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. For existing customers who has ingested custom attributes through Workforce Insights endpoint in MODS, the uploaded data will be made available to Microsoft 365 profile, Copilot experiences and Workforce Insights agent.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. The change modifies how custom organizational attributes are made available to the Workforce Insights agent and Copilot experiences.

item.title: [planForChange] Copilot Cowork: Power Platform connectors now follow Microsoft 365 admin center settings

This enables organizations to extend Cowork to third-party applications and services while giving administrators centralized control over which supported connectors can be used. Cowork respects these settings when creating connections and executing actions, helping organizations extend AI-powered business processes with enterprise-level manageability.

Organizations using Microsoft Copilot Cowork that want to use Power Platform connectors to connect Cowork with third-party applications and services.

Platforms/Services:

Microsoft Copilot Cowork, Power Platform connectors, and the Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • Administrators can allow or block supported Power Platform connectors through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Cowork respects these settings when creating connections and executing actions, including connections established before a connector was blocked.
  • Connector policies also apply to Cowork Automations.
  • Additional Power Platform connectors are being added to the Microsoft 365 admin center. Connectors become available in Cowork as they are added.

  • Configure connector availability based on your organization's requirements.

This change introduces Power Platform connector integrations between Copilot Cowork and supported third-party applications and services. Administrators can manage supported connector availability through the Microsoft 365 admin center. Power Platform admin center Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies do not apply to Cowork.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) New Outlook for Windows: All Accounts view brings email into a single inbox view
item.description:
Updated November 6, 2026: Admin controls for All Accounts view (Unified Inbox) are now available. We have added policy configuration guidance below. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

The All Accounts view, also known as Unified Inbox, lets users see email from multiple connected accounts in a single inbox view in the new Outlook for Windows without merging their mailboxes. Each account's inbox stays separate, and All Accounts view brings messages together so users can triage mail from one place.

Users can read, delete, search, move, archive, and mark messages across accounts without switching between mailboxes. The experience integrates with Copilot for AI-assisted email workflows and supports Search with Copilot for finding messages across the user's primary account.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We began rolling out in late September 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026 (previously late October).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users with more than one connected account in the new Outlook for Windows will be able to triage email across accounts from a single All Accounts view. This does not merge mailboxes or move messages between accounts. Each account remains separate, and All Accounts view provides a unified view only.

All Accounts view is enabled by default for eligible users. Users can change this setting unless their organization enforces a configuration through the admin policy described below.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required unless you want to manage this experience for your users. 

The policy “Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows” is now available through the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at config.office.com. Admins can configure whether All Accounts view is enabled or disabled by default and whether users can change that setting. The policy can be applied to selected groups. 

If the policy is not configured, All Accounts view remains enabled by default, and users can turn it off or back on. Admins who want to disable it and prevent users from enabling it must set “Configure the unified inbox view” to Disabled and “Allow user to override this setting” to Disabled. 

To configure the policy: 

  1. Go to config.office.com and open Customization > Policy Management. 
  2. Create or edit a policy configuration and scope it to the group you want to manage. 
  3. Find “Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows” and set Configuration setting to Enabled. 
  4. Under “Configure the unified inbox view,” select Enabled to show All Accounts view by default, or Disabled to keep account inboxes separate by default. 
  5. Under “Allow user to override this setting,” select Enabled to let users change the configured behavior, or Disabled to prevent changes. 
  6. Review and publish the policy configuration.

[Compliance considerations:]

This feature provides a unified view across connected accounts in the new Outlook for Windows but does not merge mailboxes or move messages between accounts. Review your organization's Outlook account and automated-assistance policies as appropriate.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft OneNote: Multimodal recording in Copilot Notebooks on Windows
item.description:

[What and why]

We are introducing multimodal capture in Copilot Notebooks on Windows. This feature enables users to capture audio, images, and notes in a single experience and use Microsoft 365 Copilot to generate structured insights such as summaries, decisions, and action items. This helps users turn meetings, conversations, and offline work into actionable outputs within Copilot Notebooks.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 566322.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning end of November 2026 (previously end of October) and expected to complete end of November 2026 (previously end of October) 

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with access to Copilot Notebooks in OneNote
  • Requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license
  • Available to commercial Microsoft 365 users with work or school (Entra ID) accounts
  • Users must have the Microsoft 365 desktop apps installed on Windows (including OneNote)

Platforms/Services

  • OneNote (desktop app on Windows)
  • Copilot Notebooks
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Users can capture audio, images, and notes directly into Copilot Notebooks.
  • Capture can be suggested or initiated when supported browser-based meetings are detected (Zoom, Webex, Google Meet).
  • Users can also manually start capture from the OneNote system tray icon.
  • Copilot generates a structured Copilot Page with insights, decisions, and action items based on captured content.
  • Captured content is saved to the selected Copilot Notebook and is available across endpoints.
  • The feature is available by default for eligible users.

[Action Required or Recommendations]

No action is required.

Admins can disable this feature using a policy setting.

  • Review available policy settings if you want to disable the feature.
  • Inform users about organizational policies related to transcription and consent.
  • Organizations should ensure users follow applicable consent and recording policies before capturing or transcribing conversations.

Learn more: 

  • Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Security for Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Yes. Captured audio, images, and notes are stored in the user’s selected Copilot Notebook (SharePoint or OneDrive).
Does the change alter how customer data is processed?Yes. Content is transcribed and processed by Microsoft 365 Copilot to generate structured insights.
Does the change introduce AI capabilities interacting with data?Yes. Copilot analyzes captured content to generate summaries, decisions, and action items.
Does the change provide new interaction with generative AI?Yes. Users interact with Copilot-generated outputs based on captured multimodal data.
Does the change add a third party integration?Yes. Supports capture from browser-based meetings including Zoom, Webex, and Google Meet.
Does the change include admin control?Yes. Admins can disable the feature using a policy setting.

  • All Microsoft Teams users in Microsoft 365 tenants, including Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, and DoD

    • Enabled by default.
    • Muted chats that are not in Favorites or user‑created sections automatically move to this section.
    • The section appears at the bottom of the chat list.
    • Unread chats continue to appear bold.
  • Meeting chats section

  • Users can drag and drop these sections to reorder them.
  • There are no admin controls for these sections.

No admin action is required.

You may want to:

  • Inform users that new chat sections are available and that they can turn them on or off.

  • Direct users to Settings > Chats and channels to manage these sections.
